articles.title: A rare gold coin from the reign of England’s Edward III, minted as a ‘leopard’ that was in circulation for just seven months in the 14th century, emerged from an ordinary suburban home and has sold at auction for £70,000
articles.summary: A rare 14th-century English gold coin that circulated for only seven months has sold for £70,000 at auction, after emerging from an ordinary suburban home.
articles.body: A rare 14th-century English gold coin that circulated for only seven months has sold for £70,000 at auction, after emerging from an ordinary suburban home. According to Antiques Trade Gazette, the coin, known as a leopard and issued during the reign of King Edward III, was sold by Essex Coin Auctions on September 30, 2026, attracting competing bids from online and telephone buyers. Two telephone bidders contested the lot in the final stages, pushing it to its reported hammer price of £70,000.The coin’s short time in circulation is central to its historical significance. Edward III, who ruled England from 1327 to 1377, introduced a series of gold coins in 1344 as England sought to strengthen its own currency and support trade. The experiment included the double leopard, leopard and half-leopard. However, the coins were abandoned within months and replaced by a different gold denomination, the noble.Why Edward III introduced the gold leopardThe British Museum’s historical record explains that England’s move towards gold coinage was driven partly by the needs of international commerce. During the 1340s, gold coins from France and Florence were already widely used, and England wanted its own currency to play a stronger role in trade. Parliament petitioned Edward III to introduce gold coins, with the new denominations ordered in December 1343.The designs also carried political meaning. According to the British Museum, the gold florin featured the king seated with an orb and sceptre, flanked by two heraldic English leopards. A Gothic canopy and fleurs-de-lis appeared in the design, while the inscription included Edward’s claim to the French throne. These elements reflected the political ambitions that formed part of the backdrop to the Hundred Years’ War between England and France.The name “leopard” referred to the heraldic animals depicted on the coinage. The denominations included a double leopard, also known as a double florin, alongside the smaller leopard and half-leopard. The coins were made of gold and represented an effort to establish an English alternative to foreign currency used by merchants.A currency experiment that lasted only monthsDespite the ambition behind the launch, the leopard coinage proved unsuccessful. The British Museum notes that the new currency was overvalued, meaning its face value was higher than the value of the gold it contained. Its denominations also did not fit comfortably into England’s existing monetary system, making the coins less practical for everyday use.The Numismatic Guaranty Company (NGC), an organisation specialising in coin grading and authentication, says Edward III’s gold leopard coinage was struck between January and July 1344. The coins were then abandoned in favour of the gold noble, which became a more successful denomination. The leopard coins were officially demonetised on August 20, 1344.The noble was valued at six shillings and eight pence, equivalent to a third of a pound. The Royal Mint’s historical guide describes it as the first English gold coin to become firmly established in circulation. It was issued alongside half-nobles and quarter-nobles, and its design and usefulness helped it remain in circulation for far longer than the short-lived leopard series.The leopard’s brief lifespan helps explain its rarity today. NGC notes that relatively few gold leopard coins were struck and that many were probably melted down after the currency was withdrawn. Coins that survived the transition are now important examples of an early attempt to introduce a lasting English gold currency.A rare survivor attracts collectorsThe £70,000 sale reported by Antiques Trade Gazette illustrates the interest that such surviving pieces can attract in the collectables market. The publication reported that the coin was offered by Essex Coin Auctions on September 30, with a 22% buyer’s premium applying to the sale. It described the £70,000 result as the hammer price, so the figure should not automatically be treated as the buyer’s total bill after the premium.The report said bidding came from both online and telephone participants, with two telephone bidders competing towards the end. The coin’s emergence from a suburban home adds an unexpected element to the story, although the available report does not establish further details about the circumstances of its discovery. It would therefore be inaccurate to assume that it was found by a metal detectorist or to attribute a specific discovery date without additional evidence.Other surviving coins from Edward III’s gold coinage have also drawn attention. NGC records that two examples of the double leopard were found in the River Tyne by schoolchildren in 1857 and later entered the British Museum’s collection. A third known example was discovered by a metal detectorist in southern England in 2006 and sold at auction that year. These are separate coins from the one reported in the 2026 Essex auction.The British Museum’s records provide a further reminder of the coinage’s historical importance: Edward III’s gold florin was part of an attempt to support trade and strengthen the kingdom’s monetary system, even though the initial design and valuation failed to win lasting acceptance.You use AI every day. articles.title: A federal judge ruled Trump-appointed prosecutor Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as Los Angeles's top U.S. attorney and disqualified him from two cases, but paused the disqualification while the Justice Department seeks a stay
articles.summary: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli has been serving unlawfully as Los Angeles’ top federal prosecutor.
articles.body: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli has been serving unlawfully as Los Angeles’ top federal prosecutor. The ruling represents a legal setback for the Justice Department’s effort to preserve Essayli’s authority, but it does not immediately remove Essayli from his position. Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright instead temporarily delayed the practical effect of his ruling, giving federal prosecutors five business days to ask for a stay while they pursue an appeal. The ruling was reported by the Los Angeles Times, The Guardian and CBS News Los Angeles, all of which describe a court order that challenges the legal arrangement used to keep Essayli in charge of one of the nation’s largest federal judicial districts.The dispute centers on Essayli’s authority to lead the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California, which covers Los Angeles and six other counties. Judge Seabright concluded that Essayli is unlawfully serving as a “de facto” United States attorney, even though his official title is first assistant U.S. attorney. In practical terms, the judge found that the Justice Department gave Essayli powers so broad that he effectively occupied the top job without holding it lawfully. “In sum, Essayli is unlawfully serving as a ‘de facto’ United States Attorney,” Seabright wrote, according to the Los Angeles Times.The ruling does not mean Essayli has been removed from office today. Judge Seabright ordered that Essayli be disqualified from participating in or supervising two criminal prosecutions, including overseeing the lawyers working on those matters. However, the judge paused that disqualification while the government prepares its expected request for a stay pending appeal. CBS News reported that the government has five business days to file that request, and that the disqualifications would take effect one week later if the request is denied, unless a higher court intervenes.What the ruling meansThe two cases affected involve Jaime Hector Ramirez, who is charged with being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, and Tu Anh Tran, who is charged with possessing property stolen from interstate or foreign shipment. Judge Seabright barred Essayli from taking part in or supervising those prosecutions. That means he cannot direct the attorneys handling the cases or otherwise exercise authority over them while the disqualification remains in place. The Los Angeles Times and CBS News both reported that the judge rejected requests to dismiss the indictments against Ramirez and Tran.That distinction matters. The judge found a problem with Essayli’s authority, but he did not conclude that the underlying criminal cases must collapse. Seabright said the defendants had not shown the substantial prejudice needed to justify dismissing the indictments. In other words, the ruling removes Essayli from a supervisory role in two prosecutions, but it leaves the charges themselves intact for now.Essayli responded to the decision by saying that his office respectfully disagreed with the order. He argued that the president and attorney general have the right to choose supervisors within the Justice Department. “Ultimately, this question will be decided by the Supreme Court, and I look forward to serving in my current role until then,” Essayli said, according to CBS News. His comments make clear that the administration views the issue as far from settled and expects it to move toward the nation’s highest court.Why the appointment is contestedThe legal fight began after Essayli was sworn in as interim U.S. attorney for the Central District of California in April 2025. When he approached the 120-day limit for serving in that temporary role, he resigned and was then appointed by Attorney General Pam Bondi as a special attorney and first assistant U.S. attorney. The Justice Department used that arrangement to allow him to continue leading the office as acting U.S. attorney. The Los Angeles Times reported that Judge Seabright rejected a similar maneuver last year, though he initially allowed Essayli to keep supervising prosecutions in his other roles.The Justice Department later revised Essayli’s delegation of authority, excluding certain powers that federal law reserves for a Senate-confirmed U.S. attorney. Government lawyers argued that this change placed Essayli’s authority on the permissible side of the legal line. Judge Seabright was not persuaded. He found that the revision made no meaningful difference because the withheld powers could not lawfully have been delegated to Essayli in the first place. “Withholding the three specific statutory powers mentioned in the revised designation order in reality withholds nothing,” the judge wrote, according to the Los Angeles Times.The ruling also follows a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit in a similar Nevada case involving prosecutor Sigal Chattah. That appeals court held that the Justice Department cannot keep an unconfirmed official in charge of a U.S. attorney’s office simply by changing the person’s title while giving them the full powers of the job. The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to review the Nevada decision, arguing that federal law permits the attorney general to delegate the powers of a vacant office and install a first assistant as its acting leader. The Supreme Court has not yet said whether it will hear the case.A wider fight over prosecutorsThe Los Angeles case is part of a broader national dispute over how the Trump administration has installed chosen prosecutors without Senate confirmation. The Los Angeles Times noted that former New Jersey prosecutor Alina Habba stepped down after an appeals court found her appointment unlawful. In Virginia, a judge’s finding that Lindsey Halligan was unlawfully appointed led to the dismissal of indictments against former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Those cases have made the question of temporary prosecutor appointments unusually consequential.For now, the immediate consequence in Los Angeles is narrow but consequential. Essayli remains in his role, but a federal judge has found that his authority to lead the office is legally flawed. If the government fails to obtain a stay, he will be barred from the Ramirez and Tran cases, although the office itself will continue operating. The Los Angeles Times reported that President Trump had still not nominated anyone to serve as U.S. attorney for the Central District of California as of Tuesday’s ruling.Defense lawyer H. Dean Steward, who filed a renewed challenge to Essayli’s authority in August, welcomed the ruling. He called it “a victory for the rule of law and the U.S. Constitution” and accused the Trump administration of ignoring the laws governing the appointment of U.S. attorneys. His comments, reported by the Los Angeles Times, reflect the view of critics who say the administration has used title changes and delegated authority to avoid the Senate confirmation process.The next step will determine whether the disqualification takes effect in the two cases, while the broader question of Essayli’s authority to lead the office remains contested. The Justice Department can ask Judge Seabright to stay the disqualification while it appeals, and the case may ultimately reach the Supreme Court alongside the related Nevada dispute. Until then, the ruling leaves unresolved whether a revised title and delegated authority can lawfully sustain Essayli’s leadership of the office. The Los Angeles Times, The Guardian and CBS News all frame the decision as part of an unresolved constitutional battle over who may lead federal prosecutor offices and under what legal authority.Note: This article is based on the court’s October 27, 2026 order. The government may still seek a stay, which could change how and when the ruling takes effect.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Barnsley chip shop owner honoured with painting by royal artist
articles.summary: Pindy Kaur, who runs Monk Bretton's Ocean Fish Bar, is immortalised by Nicky Philipps.
articles.body:
A fish and chip shop owner has been immortalised by a royal portrait artist as part of an exhibition to honour the impact independent businesses have on their communities.

Pindy Kaur has been depicted by artist Nicky Philipps, who has previously painted members of the Royal Family, including the late Queen Elizabeth II in 2013, 2016 and 2018.

Kaur, who runs Monk Bretton's Ocean Fish Bar, in Barnsley, said: "To have me painted by someone that's painted the Queen, it's just amazing."

The portrait is part of the Local Royalty campaign by Coca-Cola GB, and will go on show from 28 October at the Saatchi Gallery in London.

Kaur, 56, has been serving up fish and chips to the people of Barnsley since the early 2000s.

"Slowly, we made a friendship with the community and now everybody knows me and I know them," she said.

"I've watched their kids grow up and everything. It's just lovely to have that community around you."

Asked how she felt when she first saw the painting she said she "couldn't believe it", describing it as "beautiful".

Philipps said she thought the decision to recognise "the real champions of their communities" was "a lovely idea".

She the process of painting Kaur and members of the Royal Family was "exactly the same".

"Your end goal is the same: to try and capture something of the character," she said.

She added that Kaur's job was "a hell of a lot more important than my job and she clearly does it really well".

articles.body: Malaysian customs authorities have seized advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth about $12.1 million concealed inside 30 server units at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, as investigators close in on a suspected syndicate believed to be smuggling high-performance semiconductors through the country, as reported by Reuters. The seizure comes amid heightened scrutiny of the movement of advanced AI chips, particularly those originating from the United States, after Malaysia introduced export controls last year following pressure from Washington to curb the flow of sensitive technology into China.Falsely declared as electronic componentsAspalila said the servers were falsely declared as electronic components and shipped through Malaysia so that no restrictions would apply when they were exported to the next destination. Initial investigations found that the shipment came from an Asian country and was due to be re-exported to another country in the region, a move that required a trade permit. That permit is required under Malaysia’s Strategic Trade Act 2010. Aspalila declined to say where the servers came from, where the chips were made or where they were headed.A suspected syndicate and a local firmAs per the Reuters report, at least five cases have been linked to the syndicate, involving seizures of chips worth more than 100 million ringgit in total, she said, adding that she could not give more details because the investigation is continuing. TRT World, citing officials, described the latest bust as the fifth case this year involving a syndicate smuggling advanced AI chips, with the total value above $24 million. A Malaysian company that helped facilitate the shipment has been called in to assist with the investigation. In June 2026, airport officers seized 72 server units under similar false declarations, valued at about $12.93 million.Probe focuses on wider networkCustoms investigators suspect the shipment is linked to a broader smuggling network responsible for a similar attempt that authorities intercepted in June. According to officials, at least five cases have been connected to the suspected syndicate, involving seizures of semiconductors worth more than 100 million ringgit in total. Authorities declined to provide additional details because of the ongoing investigationExport controls on US-origin chipsThe seizure comes against the backdrop of Malaysia’s export controls on advanced AI chips. Malaysia imposed controls last year on the movement of US-origin advanced AI chips, after pressure from the United States to stem their flow into China. The case shows how customs officials are looking closely at the servers that contain chips, their declared classification and their intended destinations, as well as at the chips themselves, according to StratNews Global. Malaysia has also opened several investigations, including one into how servers containing US-made Nvidia chips bound for Singapore ended up in Malaysia.The case highlights the increasing importance of export controls surrounding advanced AI hardware, which is critical for training and running sophisticated AI models. Malaysia tightened regulations on the movement of US-origin AI chips in 2025 as governments stepped up efforts to monitor the global trade of high-performance semiconductors.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nepal faces days of rain, snow and storms as Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recording up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm’s impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall from Thursday.The Nepal Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecasting Division said the country was currently experiencing the partial influence of westerly winds, with the approaching cyclone expected to bring widespread precipitation and a risk of heavy rain and snowfall through the weekend.“The country is currently under the partial influence of westerly winds. In addition, the country is expected to come under the influence of Cyclone ‘Arnab’, developed over the Bay of Bengal, from Kartik 12 (Thursday),” the department said in its latest bulletin.Weather conditions remained relatively clear in the Himalayan and hilly regions on Wednesday morning, although fog and mist affected parts of the Terai, valleys and river basins.The department forecast increasing cloud cover and scattered precipitation from Wednesday afternoon, with conditions becoming more unsettled overnight. Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces are among the areas expected to experience rain, while snowfall is possible in Himalayan regions.The risk is forecast to increase on Thursday night, when thunderstorms and lightning could accompany rain and snowfall. Heavy precipitation is possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, while some areas of Lumbini could also receive heavy rainfall.Friday and Saturday are expected to bring the most widespread impacts. The department warned that heavy rain or snowfall could affect several provinces, with isolated locations facing the possibility of very heavy precipitation.Its Friday forecast states, “Mostly cloudy throughout the country. Light to moderate rain or snowfall accompanied by thunder and lightning is possible at most places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces and at many places in Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces.”The expected combination of westerly winds and moisture associated with Cyclone Arnab could increase the risk of flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in vulnerable hilly regions. Heavy snowfall could also create hazardous conditions in high-altitude areas.Meanwhile, in India, at least three people died in cyclone Arnab-related incidents in Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday. South Coast Railway (SCoR) cancelled 57 trains and rescheduled 15 others as a precautionary measure. However, officials quoted by ANI said the cyclone had weakened from a very severe to a severe cyclonic storm after moving over land, and was expected to weaken further. Four additional NDRF teams were deployed to Andhra Pradesh.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Spain train collision: Several killed; rescue operations on; what we know so far
articles.summary: At least 50 people were killed after two high-speed trains collided in Spain’s central Toledo province on Wednesday, local media reported.
articles.body: At least 50 people were killed after two high-speed trains collided in Spain’s central Toledo province on Wednesday, local media reported. A trainee railway worker who had gone missing following the crash has since been confirmed dead, while the driver of an AVE high-speed train remains unaccounted for, according to Spanish media reports.The collision occurred shortly after 9 am local time on the Madrid-Seville line, near the town of Urda. A Renfe train struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train, causing two carriages to derail, with some reportedly falling down an embankment. Emergency services rushed to the scene as rescue teams worked to reach passengers trapped inside the damaged coaches. What happened?Spain’s rail infrastructure operator Adif confirmed that traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line had been suspended following the collision. The accident involved a Renfe AVE service and an Iryo train travelling in the same direction towards southern Spain.According to Castilla-La Mancha regional government spokesperson Esther Padilla, the Renfe train was carrying 397 passengers, while the Iryo service had 147 passengers on board, including a baby. This puts the total number of passengers at 544.Initial reports from Spanish newspaper El País suggested that the collision may have resulted from human error following a failure in the main signalling system. Government sources cited by the newspaper said the system had switched to manual operation after the failure, leaving several trains halted in the area.An operator at Madrid’s Atocha control centre allegedly instructed the Renfe train to proceed despite the Iryo train obstructing the track, according to the preliminary account. These claims remain subject to investigation, and authorities have not officially established the cause of the crash. Rescue operations underway, driver still missingEmergency services deployed medical helicopters and mobilised hospitals in Toledo and Alcázar de San Juan to treat the injured. Rescue teams focused on the two most severely damaged carriages, where passengers were trapped amid twisted metal and wreckage.Health Minister Mónica García said the impact had been severe and warned that the situation could worsen as rescue operations continued. Injured passengers were being transferred to hospitals according to the seriousness of their conditions.Passenger and journalist Miguel Ángel Pérez Laguna told Spanish broadcaster Capital Radio that the impact was extremely strong, describing how the train’s interior was thrown from side to side.The mayor of nearby Urda, Manuel Galán, said emergency services had asked the local council to prepare a sports pavilion to accommodate passengers and those requiring assistance. Regional president Emiliano García-Page also travelled to the crash site as authorities coordinated the response.Also read: Spain train crash: Govt blames 'human error' by operator — what led to collision? Not Spain’s first rail tragedy this yearThe collision is the latest major railway disaster to hit Spain this year. In January, a high-speed train derailed near Adamuz in Córdoba province and collided with an oncoming Renfe train, killing 46 people and injuring hundreds, according to reports at the time.That disaster triggered scrutiny of railway maintenance and infrastructure investment, as well as concerns about the safety of Spain’s extensive high-speed rail network. The latest collision, involving trains operated by Renfe and Iryo, has renewed those concerns.Investigators will now seek to establish what caused Wednesday’s crash, including whether the reported signalling failure and possible human error contributed to the collision.Also read: At least 50 killed as high-speed train rams another in Spain's Toledo; videos show gutted carriagesYou use AI every day. articles.title: A Washington couple with seven children placed a $500,000 house in a trust before divorcing; the wife received a $735,000 Sequim home, and an October 27 court upheld the decision not to require refinancing
articles.summary: A divorce involving a Washington couple with seven children has highlighted how courts can divide family property and mortgage obligations without
articles.body: A divorce involving a Washington couple with seven children has highlighted how courts can divide family property and mortgage obligations without requiring a spouse to refinance a home. The Washington Court of Appeals, Division Two, ruled on October 27, 2026, that a lower court acted within its discretion when it awarded the family’s Sequim home to Megan Mae Coelho and assigned the remaining mortgage debt to her without requiring her to refinance the loan or sell the property within a specified period. According to the unpublished opinion available on Justia, her former husband, Benjamin A Mavy, challenged the arrangement, arguing that he remained financially exposed to a mortgage on a home he no longer owned.Couple transferred property into a trust before divorceMavy and Coelho married in 2002 and had seven children during their marriage. Before moving to Washington, the family lived in Wyoming, where the couple received $1,518,103 in September 2021 for their interest in a business in which Mavy had been involved. In November 2021, the couple established an irrevocable trust under Wyoming law for asset protection and estate planning. They transferred personal property valued at $125,000 and an additional $250,000 into the trust. Their Wyoming home, valued at approximately $500,000, was also held in the trust, with their children named as beneficiaries.Mavy served as the trust adviser and retained substantial control over the trust’s assets, including the ability to determine whether the property could be used by either spouse. The couple subsequently moved to Washington and purchased a home in Sequim. Mavy filed for divorce in November 2022. The division of property became one of several disputed issues during the proceedings.Divorce court awarded the Sequim home to the wifeFollowing a trial in August 2024, the lower court issued findings on the couple’s property, debts and parenting arrangements. It awarded the Sequim home to Coelho and assigned the debt secured by the property to her. The final divorce order, entered on December 12, 2024, recorded approximately $300,000 in equity in the Sequim property and an outstanding mortgage balance of $428,572. The court did not require Coelho to refinance the loan or sell the home within a specified period.The order also gave Mavy access to the mortgage account for as long as his name remained on the loan, allowing him to monitor whether payments were being made on time. In addition, it required Coelho to hold him harmless if her failure to pay an assigned debt resulted in a creditor pursuing him for payment. The court ordered Coelho to pay Mavy a further $50,000. It also divided the couple’s community interests in four businesses equally, with each receiving half of the shares or units classified as community property. The lower court concluded that the overall division of property and debts was just and equitable. It separately determined that it lacked jurisdiction to divide the Wyoming real estate held by the trust.Husband challenged the mortgage arrangementMavy appealed the property division, arguing that awarding Coelho the Sequim home without requiring her to refinance left him exposed to a debt from which he no longer benefited. He disputed the lower court’s assessment that the arrangement presented “little to no risk” to him. His argument focused on the possibility that he could remain liable to the mortgage lender even though Coelho had received the property and was responsible for its payments under the divorce order.The lower court had based its assessment on the equity in the Sequim home, Mavy’s ability to monitor timely mortgage payments and the provision requiring Coelho to protect him against collection arising from debts assigned to her. Mavy also challenged other aspects of the divorce proceedings, including the property division’s finality and the denial of his request to hold Coelho in contempt. His challenges to the original parenting plan and relocation order were rendered moot after the trial court entered a new parenting plan in May 2026 and a new relocation order in July 2026.Appeals court upheld the lower court’s decisionThe Court of Appeals concluded that Mavy had not demonstrated that the evidence failed to support the lower court’s findings. It upheld the property division and the denial of his contempt motion, while ruling that his challenges to the earlier parenting plan and relocation order were moot. The appeals court emphasised the broad discretion trial courts have when distributing property during a divorce. Washington law requires a just and equitable division, but that does not necessarily mean an equal division or require a particular method of handling mortgage debt.The court therefore affirmed the challenged decisions, including the award of the Sequim home to Coelho without a refinancing deadline. The ruling did not remove Mavy from the mortgage; rather, it upheld the divorce court’s decision not to make refinancing a condition of Coelho receiving the property. The October 27 opinion illustrates the distinction between assigning responsibility for a mortgage between divorcing spouses and requiring a lender to release a borrower from the loan. The court upheld the specific arrangement in this case, based on the evidence and protections included in the divorce order.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Russell Brand tells court allegations made friends and colleagues turn against him
articles.summary: The entertainer is giving evidence at his trial on charges including rape and assault, which he denies.
articles.body:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

The entertainer began giving evidence on Wednesday as his defence case got under way at his trial at Southwark Crown Court in London.

Brand, 51, is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one charge of attempted indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies all the charges.

Asked whether consent was important to him, he told the court: "Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed in many ways more important than sex itself."

After Brand entered the witness box on Wednesday morning, defence barrister Ian Winter KC began by taking him through the indictment, asking him if he had committed the offences.

After each question, Brand replied "no" loudly towards the jury.

Brand was then asked about a documentary that aired in 2023, which included some allegations against him.

Asked by Winter what impact the documentary had had on his friends and colleagues turning their backs on him, Brand said: "It was devastating."

Winter questioned whether Brand had been able to persuade any friend or acquaintance who might have been able to give evidence on his behalf to appear in court.

Brand replied: "I have not." Winter asked: "Will they touch you with a bargepole?" Brand said: "No."

The actor and comedian was standing tall in the witness box with his hands clasped behind his back. He was wearing a dark navy suit with his curly hair resting on his shoulders.

Brand also claimed in court that he was told he could not stay with his son at Great Ormond Street hospital in London when the child was having open heart surgery, following the documentary and a newspaper investigation.

He told the court: "Due to material that had been published in the public eye they had to bar my attendance and presence.

"They were unclear about what legal reason there was but that was the reason they gave to my wife Laura and I."

Brand told the court: "My entire life has been consumed by these allegations," adding that he had "devoted myself to these matters".

Winter asked Brand if he recalled meeting the first complainant, who alleges he raped her at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999.

Brand said yes, explaining that he found her "loquacious" and "interesting".

When asked if there was any truth in the allegations that he raped her, he said: "No."

Under cross examination, the prosecution suggested Brand "just didn't care whether she was interested in having sex with you or not". Brand rejected that, saying he did care "very much".

Asked whether he was sure he "didn't think no means yes", he replied: "I know what no means."

Brand was then asked about another woman, who alleges that the entertainer grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet and raping her.

Brand said he recalled been invited to a party in London at a bar in 2004, and said a friend had introduced him to the complainant by saying "something like 'there's a bird here who really wants to meet you mate'."

When asked if he remembered what he said to her upon meeting, he told the court: "I would have said something like, 'You're really, really beautiful'."

The barrister asked whether he had grabbed her breasts. "Absolutely not," Brand replied.

When questioned if he would have behaved in the way that had been alleged, he said it would have amounted to "disgusting behaviour".

"I was increasingly focused on my promiscuity," he said. "That's not the way I would have behaved because it's not only criminal but vulgar."

Brand said he remembered going into the toilet with her but said "no" when asked if he had dragged or forced her there.

"Did your penis enter her mouth at all whilst in the cubicle?" Winter asked. "No," said Brand.

Another complainant, who worked at MTV, alleges that Brand tried to drag her into a toilet at work in 2001.

At the time, he was one of the channel's star presenters. She said she managed to wrench herself away.

Asked if he had intended a non-consensual sexual encounter, Brand told the court: "Absolutely not."

In relation to another woman, who accuses Brand of anal rape, he said he remembered her being in his dressing room at the Hammersmith Apollo theatre in London in 2009 after his comedy show.

He said after a "memorable" sexual encounter, he contacted her again to try to meet, adding: "I was excited and enthusiastic about it."

Brand also said he had saved her number in his phone using a code, saying: "That was what I used to denote casual hook-ups and women I met I could hook up with."

After inviting her to his house in Hampstead, he said they had consensual sex in his room.

When asked if he committed anal rape, he said no. When asked if she had asked him to stop, he said no.

Asked by the prosecution later if his memory was "a little selective" in what he could remember, Brand replied: "No."

The prosecution suggested Brand only remembered certain parts of his encounters after being interviewed by the police and viewing the women's evidence.

"You saw the evidence and started to remember. You pretended you couldn't remember the encounters until the police found photos and negatives," the prosecution said.

Brand denied that was the case and said he was straining every sinew to recall distant events but was struggling to do so.

He was also asked on Wednesday about his wedding to singer Katy Perry in October 2010 and whether it brought a "sea change" to his life. He said the marriage brought him "staggering fame".

Being cross examined, Brand agreed with the prosecution's suggestion that he blamed Channel 4 documentary programme Dispatches for the allegations.

Asked if the media had been fair to him, Brand said he "would reject that suggestion strongly".

Under intense questioning from prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC, Brand denied pretending to be gay in his pursuit of women, after one of the complainants said they assumed he was gay and that she had felt "sexually safe with him".

Brand also told the jury he had an obsession with sex as a younger man but denied giving himself a "goal" to sleep with 5,000 women.

The comedian's former friend and flatmate, Mark Pinheiro, previously told the jury that Brand had boasted on a car journey to the Labour Party conference in 1999 about his techniques for "pulling" women and allegedly revealed an ambition to sleep with 5,000 women.

Asked about the alleged claim, Brand told the jury: "While I don't remember, it's entirely possible it's the kind of badinage [banter] I would have engaged in when I was 24."

Brand admitted he was "obsessed" with sex in his younger years but denied the extent of the impact on his life.

From the witness box, he said consent was "non-negotiable".

articles.title: Popular Christian YouTuber releases biblical fantasy novel meant to challenge today’s dark content
articles.summary: Popular Christian YouTuber releases biblical fantasy novel, says Hollywood needs less “Game of Thrones" and more “Narnia"
articles.body: Bible teacher and popular YouTuber Daniel Maritz is now sharing his take on the battle between light and darkness as the new co-author of the biblical fantasy novel "Lightborn: Dawn of Darkness." Maritz, who co-wrote the book with his brother Hernu, described the novel as the first in a larger saga centered on a world before the biblical flood, where ancient history and mythology intertwine. There, the main character — born a slave and named Uldako — seeks to uncover the deeper truths about his world, his heritage and the war behind all wars. He walks a path of survival, pursued by beasts, scorched by loss and drawn toward an ancient prophecy involving the Lightborn. MEL GIBSON SAYS 'MONSTER' EPIC 'PASSION' SEQUEL SPANS SPIRITUAL REALMS — AND THIS TIME, IT'S IN ENGLISH If it sounds like a video game, Maritz and his brother would likely agree. In fact, the two also plan to create a companion video game based on the book through their company, Ruach Entertainment. "Both of which are meant to relate to what’s happening in the world today — in culture, entertainment and basically everything that’s around us," Maritz told Fox News Digital, noting that although the story is ancient, it is still relevant today. "There is not only a battle between light and darkness in Hollywood, but also in education, religion and culture in general." 'WIZARDS OF WAVERLY PLACE' STAR DAVID HENRIE SAYS HIS FAITH COST HIM AGENTS, MONEY AND FRIENDS IN HOLLYWOOD In a recent Fox News Digital opinion piece, Maritz pointed out that darker content is actually "a distraction from the good of fantasy: the imagined worlds, heroes and adventures that call fans to a higher ethos." Maritz, who is from South Africa, grew up as the youngest of five children. He has spoken about two of his brothers who died, including one who was murdered in Johannesburg and another who was killed following a car crash. It was while sitting by his brother Etienne’s side in the hospital that Maritz experienced an awakening of sorts. He recalled hearing a voice ask him, "Daniel, where would you have gone if you died?" That’s when he knew he wanted to create stories for today that look back to the lessons of the Bible in a world oversaturated with violence and darkness. "So entertainment changes not just the West, but culture as we know it today. And so we have a lot of shows like ‘Game of Thrones' and other shows that bring a lot of vulgar scenes into them and a lot of cussing," Maritz explained. NETFLIX FACES TURMOIL AS GRETA GERWIG'S $280 MILLION 'NARNIA' MOVIE LOOKS HEADED FOR DISASTER Maritz modeled his book after works such as C.S. Lewis’ "The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe," which is deeply infused with Christian theology while serving as a rich Christian allegory and J.R.R. Tolkien’s "The Lord of the Rings," which is also rooted in Christian theology. According to Maritz, today’s society is addicted to entertainment and what he describes as "the evil side of it." FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT "It’s through entertainment, through politics and education that they mostly try to change culture as we know it," he said. "And I think people are waking up and getting tired of it — especially when they start changing stories that we know were written by great writers like C.S. Lewis. We know that he wrote the character of Aslan to represent Jesus in this world." In terms of adapting "Lightborn: Dawn of Darkness" into an interactive experience, Maritz, whose YouTube channels include DLM Christian Lifestyle and DLM Christian Perspective, wants it to serve as an alternative to more violent video games. SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’ "We’ve got to share the Gospel because there are 3.5 billion gamers in the world. This industry is bigger than the music and film industries combined. But there’s just darkness in there," Maritz said, noting that many young people use video games as an escape. "Today’s games are just a different form of storytelling, but they let you engage with it." As he wrote in his Fox News Digital piece, "The question, then, is not whether evil exists, but whether fantasy creators ask their video game players to fight it or practice it, whether fantasy authors craft stories that expose darkness or train an audience to enjoy it." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "To every storyteller reading this: The desire for wonder without wreckage is enormous. We need to craft worlds worth losing ourselves in for an afternoon, with heroes worth following into the dark because we trust they’re going to lead us back into the light," he wrote.

articles.title: Spain high-speed railway crash kills at least 68 after train stopped on tracks
articles.summary: A high-speed RENFE train slammed into a stopped IRYO train in Toledo province, derailing two cars and killing at least 68 people on Wednesday.
articles.body: A high-speed train collision killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday when one train collided with another that had stopped on the tracks, derailing both trains and shredding at least two cabins. The crash took place in Spain's Castilla-La Mancha, with the regional government confirming the death toll and adding that another 58 people required medical treatment in hospitals. Rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies, with witnesses describing a gruesome scene. Wednesday's incident is the second high-speed rail crash Spain has suffered this year. Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the regional government, said the cause of the crash is not yet known. Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Both trains were carrying hundreds of passengers, and were headed in the same direction on a route from Madrid to Seville. CRASH INVOLVING SPEEDING TRAIN, MINIBUS IN BELGIUM LEAVES 4 DEAD INCLUDING 2 CHILDREN One train, run by the state-owned RENFE company, ran into the tail of the other train owned by private company IRYO that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track. Those companies were the same ones involved in January's crash. Padilla said 397 passengers were on the RENFE train and 147 passengers on the IRYO train. David Gómez, a construction worker, was working with his brother and another colleague nearby when they heard the crash and ran to help, he told the newspaper El País. "People were trying to get out through the windows…. We cut through some fences to access the area and treated people with the first-aid kits we had brought," until emergency services arrived, he said. "As I was trying to pull a young woman out, there was a piece of a leg." Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged train cars. She said the injured are being sent to different hospitals in the area. BYSTANDER VIDEO CAPTURES NORFOLK SOUTHERN TRAIN T-BONING SEPTIC TRUCK AT VIRGINIA RAILROAD CROSSING "It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," García said. Passenger Ignacio Relaño was traveling on the RENFE train. He told state broadcaster TVE that the train had stopped momentarily on the line before it started again and then crashed into the IRYO. "We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact," he said. "The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cellphones. Everything shook." Another passenger recounted to Cadena Ser radio how she felt the train slam on the brakes and was thrown forward in her seat, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw body parts and trapped people covered in blood. IRYO, an Italian-owned company, said in a statement that it has "activated its security protocols and is closely working with authorities." articles.title: Cheesecake Factory among list of popular eateries in America's priciest neighborhoods
articles.summary: Cava, Shake Shack and The Cheesecake Factory top a new analysis ranking restaurant chains by home values near their locations nationwide.
articles.body: The Cheesecake Factory has been in the headlines after former President Barack Obama joked that President Donald Trump's White House décor looked "like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory." The remark sparked debate over whether the chain is a spot for everyday Americans, and a new analysis of restaurant chains near neighborhoods with higher and lower home values found where it ranks. Home values near Cheesecake Factory restaurants were about 27% higher than in areas in the same region with similar population density, partly because many of them are located in upscale malls, The Washington Sun found. 5 RESTAURANT CHAINS SERVE UP THE BEST BREAKFAST VALUE AS AMERICANS LOOK TO SAVE The outlet analyzed data from Overture Maps, Zillow and the Census Bureau using a methodology adapted from housing expert Aziz Sunderji's analysis of businesses near areas with higher and lower home values. The analysis also found that businesses such as Club Pilates, Whole Foods, Warby Parker and Apple stores were associated with neighborhoods with higher home values, while Five Below, Olive Garden, Texas Roadhouse and Planet Fitness were linked to areas with lower home values. The Cheesecake Factory ranked third among restaurant chains for the highest home values near its locations. Below are the top five, with two chains tied for fifth. 1. Cava For the fast-casual Mediterranean and Greek chain, home values within three miles of its locations were 39% higher than in areas in the same region with similar population density. It traces its roots back to 2006, when three childhood friends opened a Greek restaurant honoring their shared heritage. They began selling dips in grocery stores in 2008 and launched the fast-casual chain in 2011. BELOVED RESTAURANT CHAIN DWINDLES FROM 850 LOCATIONS TO 87, BUT EXPERT SEES 'A LOT OF LIFE LEFT' Cava celebrated its 500th store opening in September, according to a news release. 2. Shake Shack Home values near Shake Shacks were 38% higher than in similar areas. The burger chain began in 2001 as a hot dog cart in New York City's Madison Square Park, launched by restaurateur Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality Group to support a public art project. Shake Shack's popularity led to the first permanent location in 2004, according to its website. Since then, it has grown into an international fast-casual chain with hundreds of locations, known for its Angus beef burgers, crinkle-cut fries, hot dogs, chicken sandwiches and milkshakes. REGIONAL BURGER CHAINS ARE BEATING FAST-FOOD GIANTS IN ONE KEY MEASURE It helped define the mid-2010s era of premium fast-casual smash burgers. "We certainly didn't invent them — but as a category, they now seem to be everywhere," Meyer told Eater last year. 3. The Cheesecake Factory The Cheesecake Factory's roots were in Beverly Hills, California, where David Overton opened the first restaurant in 1978 to showcase his mother Evelyn's cheesecakes. She began baking cheesecakes in Detroit in the 1940s before opening a small bakery in Los Angeles in 1972. Decades later, it ranked third among restaurant chains in the analysis and has expanded to about 250 restaurants worldwide. BABY BOOMERS CROWN THEIR FAVORITE CASUAL DINING CHAIN AS GEN Z CHOOSES A DIFFERENT WINNER It has also cemented its place in American culture, synonymous with the suburban mall experience of the 1990s and 2000s and a symbol of American excess with its large portions, sprawling menu and over-the-top interior design. 4. P.F. Chang's P.F. Chang's ranked fourth among the restaurant chains, with home values within three miles of its locations 26% higher than in comparable areas. The Asian-inspired chain is known for dishes such as Chicken Lettuce Wraps and Mongolian Beef and is similarly tied to the casual-dining boom of the 1990s and 2000s. Like The Cheesecake Factory, it serves generous portions and is a fixture in malls and shopping centers, with similarly elaborate decor. "P.F. Chang's looks for vibrant destinations where guests are already gathering to shop, dine and celebrate," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "When evaluating a new location, we consider factors like visibility, accessibility, traffic patterns and the strength of the surrounding dining and retail community." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Founded in 1993 in Scottsdale, Arizona, P.F. Chang's now operates more than 300 restaurants worldwide, spanning over 20 countries. 5. Chipotle Mexican Grill and Panera Bread (tied) Chipotle Mexican Grill and Panera Bread tied for fifth, with home values within three miles of both chains' locations 17% higher than in comparable areas. Chipotle was founded near the University of Denver in 1993, serving burritos inspired by San Francisco's Mission District. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER It has since grown to more than 4,000 restaurants across several international markets, offering customizable burritos, bowls, tacos and salads. Panera started as a bakery in 1987 and has grown to more than 2,250 bakery-cafes across 48 states, Washington, D.C., and Ontario, Canada, focusing on soups, salads, sandwiches and baked goods. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Both commonly appear in suburban shopping centers and retail corridors, while Panera has announced plans to expand to locations such as hospitals and universities. articles.title: Apple News pushed 84 negative headlines about GOP priorities ahead of midterms with zero positive, study finds
articles.summary: The MRC study found Apple News promoted 84 negative headlines on Republican priorities and zero positive ones during the lead-up to midterm elections.
articles.body: Apple News promoted more than 80 stories that negatively framed the issues Republicans care about during the lead-up to the midterm elections while promoting zero positive stories about GOP-aligned issues, according to the Media Research Center (MRC). The MRC, a conservative media watchdog, analyzed Apple News’ top 20 stories from Sept. 15-30 and found that voters who rely on the platform for information were fed roughly five stories per day that negatively characterized the Republicans' top 10 policy priorities. During that same period, Apple News, which comes preinstalled on every iPhone in America, did not promote a single story that positively framed a Republican priority, according to the study. APPLE, GOOGLE NEWS ALGORITHMS SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE STORIES ON MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL EL-SAYED, STUDY SAYS "Apple News ran 84 negative headlines on Republican priorities and zero positive ones. Zero! My dentist finds more good news in a root canal," David Bozell told Fox News Digital. "Millions of voters open that app before they vote, and Apple's editors are in there like a bartender who waters down only one party's drinks," David Bozell continued. "Come on, Apple, tell us who picks these stories and why Republicans got the whole bad-news buffet." MRC staffers Luis Cornelio and Madison Van Zant, who conducted the study, wrote that their findings add to the "growing body of evidence that the platform’s editors continue to curate its feeds to push a left-wing political agenda." The MRC found that 117 stories from outlets Apple News promoted GOP-aligned issues during the review period, with 84 stories featuring negative headlines (72%) and 33 (28%) receiving neutral headlines. None of the headlines promoted by Apple News presented GOP issues in a positive light. APPLE AND GOOGLE SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE GRAHAM PLATNER STORIES FOR MONTHS ON THEIR NEWS PLATFORM, STUDY FINDS "In short, Apple News ensured that immigration was framed through court defeats and sensationalist stories; the economy through high gas prices; law and order through positive portrayals of police abolition; cuts to government through accusations of radicalism; foreign policy through portrayals of America’s adversaries as warriors; and efforts to curb waste through claims of unlawful cuts," Cornelio and Van Zant wrote. The study was conducted after the MRC identified 10 prominent Republican-aligned issues based on recent polls: immigration and border security, the economy, law and order, reducing government spending, combating drug use, national security and foreign policy, taxes, countering terrorism, education and protecting the unborn. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Apple News has long been accused of having a liberal bias, and Fox News Digital reported earlier this year that many of the company’s top executives and board members have made substantial contributions to Democrats over multiple election cycles. Some conservatives were hopeful that Apple News would pivot once new CEO John Ternus took control of the company, but a previous MRC study found that the news aggregator increased the percentage of stories from leftist outlets during his first month on the job. Apple did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Kathy Hochul 'excited' about prospect of Democrats tying Trump up in investigations
articles.summary: Kathy Hochul told Politico she's "excited" about Democrats using investigations and subpoenas to halt President Donald Trump's agenda if they retake Congress.
articles.body: Gov. Kathy Hochul, D-N.Y., told Politico Tuesday that she was "excited" at the possibility of a Democratic Congress holding up President Donald Trump's agenda through investigations and hearings. Hochul brought up the concept while discussing the Democratic Party's chances of not only retaking the House in November, but the Senate as well. With both chambers of Congress, Hochul said Democrats could halt the "corruption" she alleged was occurring under the Trump administration. "We are hoping for the House, but to get the Senate on top of it, next level, game-changing, extraordinary," Hochul said. "So, I'm excited about this. When you talk about Trump's next two years with that Democratic House and Senate, hey, guess what? There's investigations, there's hearings, there's subpoenas, there's questioning. We're putting the media spotlight on everything he's doing and trying to stop his 'flood the zone' strategy of doing so much bad stuff in such a short time that you can't even keep track of it." THE NINE KEY RACES THAT WILL DECIDE WHO CONTROLS THE SENATE, AND WHERE THEY STAND She added, "And so now you'll have congressional oversight committees and subcommittees and commissions. So that's going to tie things up to at least not that we want to stop the workings of the good part of government, but stop the corruption, stop the abuse and things that he's getting away with now. A fraction of them would have been national scandals for years and taken out here." Despite her criticism of Trump's agenda, Hochul also voiced hope that she could work with the president in his final two years in office. "I think there are some legacy projects that I've encouraged him to look at in New York as well. I want to build nuclear. I want to power this state with what'll ultimately be low-cost, reliable power," Hochul said. GOV KATHY HOCHUL SIGNS NEW YORK ONTO TRUMP'S SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DESPITE TEACHERS UNION OPPOSITION She added, "I can do nuclear and look, I committed that we're going to build more nuclear in New York than the entire country has in the last 30 years. I need the president. I have a proposal before him now, how to unlock this and do it in half the time and much less cost. I've got a plan. So, those are areas where he can make a legacy in his home state." In a statement to Fox News Digital, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said, "Democrats have no agenda to improve the lives of Americans—their only agenda is to continue their decade-long witch hunt against President Trump. This administration and commonsense Republicans will continue to secure our borders, restore law and order, putting more money back into the pockets of hard-working Americans, and deliver wins for the American people. The choice has never been clearer: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ obstruction." BRUCE BLAKEMAN HAMMERS DEM GOV HOCHUL, MAMDANI OVER SUBWAY SAFETY DURING NYC CAMPAIGN RIDE The New York Republican State Committee communications director David Laska criticized Hochul for saying the "quiet part out loud" and suggesting the Democrats' main goal is to halt the president's agenda rather than focus on the state. "Kathy Hochul said the quiet part out loud, admitting that if Democrats win control of either chamber, they'll use the powers of Congress to thwart the President's agenda with phony hearings and investigations. Kathy Hochul should worry less about President Trump and more about the fact that New York continues to lead the nation in outmigration because she keeps us the most taxed, least affordable, least free state in the nation," Laska told Fox News Digital. articles.title: An Australian man offered $10,000 to find his missing dog; then a stranger sent him an AI-generated photo of the pet in a cage in a suspected scam
articles.summary: An Australian man searching desperately for his missing dog offered a A$10,000 reward for its safe return, hoping someone would help bring his beloved pet
articles.body: An Australian man searching desperately for his missing dog offered a A$10,000 reward for its safe return, hoping someone would help bring his beloved pet home. Instead, he received a message from a stranger claiming to have found the animal, followed by a photograph that appeared to show the dog inside a cage. The promise briefly raised his hopes, but the stranger never arrived at the agreed meeting point. When the owner examined the photograph, he suspected it had been created using artificial intelligence, with an image he had previously shared online seemingly manipulated to make the dog appear inside a crate. The incident has highlighted how scammers can exploit the emotional distress of people searching for missing pets.How Bundy went missing in Western AustraliaWestyn Ruyter's 18-month-old dog, Bundy, an Irish wolfhound and blue heeler cross, disappeared on October 9 near Southampton Road in Balingup, a town in Western Australia's South West region, approximately 240 kilometres south of Perth.Ruyter had let Bundy and his two other dogs, Winnie and Runt, out on his rural property, where he was building a house. The dogs usually ran around the property before following him back.Winnie returned that evening, but Bundy and Runt remained missing. At around 1.30 am, Runt eventually returned alone. According to Ruyter, the dog appeared frightened, was shaking and seemed to have pain in his hind legs.Ruyter subsequently discovered that security cameras on the property had been stolen. However, no connection has been established between the missing cameras and Bundy's disappearance.A $10,000 reward brings a false leadAs the search continued without success, Ruyter appealed for help on social media and offered A$10,000 for Bundy's safe return.He also put up missing-dog posters and contacted veterinarians and rangers in surrounding areas. Bundy was particularly important to him because he had been with the family since birth. The dog was the puppy of Ruyter's other dog, Winnie.Ruyter described Bundy as gentle and well-behaved, saying he would do anything to bring him home.The reward attracted attention, but it also preceded an encounter that added to the owner's distress.A person contacted Ruyter claiming to have found Bundy and suggested meeting at a general store in Balingup. Believing the message could finally lead him to his dog, Ruyter arranged for his father to go to the meeting point.His father waited for approximately an hour and searched around the town, but nobody arrived with Bundy.The suspicious photograph that raised alarm bellsWhen Ruyter asked the person for further proof that Bundy had been found, the individual sent a photograph that purported to show the missing dog inside a cage.Ruyter quickly became suspicious. He said the image appeared to use the same photograph of Bundy that he had previously posted on Facebook, with a cage seemingly added around the animal.He also pointed to what he considered suspicious visual details, including an artificial-looking dog bowl and blurred cage bars in front of Bundy's face.Ruyter told ABC News that the image was obviously AI-generated. After sending it, the person stopped responding.The photograph appeared to offer evidence that Bundy had been found, but it did not establish that the sender had the dog. The available information does not identify the person behind the messages or independently establish which technology was used to create or manipulate the image. Nor does it confirm that Ruyter paid the person any money.Australian authorities warn about missing-pet scamsThe Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's National Anti-Scam Centre told ABC News that it was aware of scams targeting people searching for missing pets.According to the agency, scammers can use AI-generated images to make it appear that they have found an animal. They may then demand money, gift cards or cryptocurrency in exchange for returning the pet.The centre warned that scammers exploit situations that are urgent or emotionally distressing, making people searching for missing animals potential targets.Although this broader warning describes how missing-pet scams can operate, the available reporting does not establish that the person who contacted Ruyter demanded payment from him. His case centres on the false lead, the suspicious photograph and the sender's subsequent silence.How artificial intelligence can make scams more convincingPaul Haskell-Dowland, Professor of Cyber Security Practice at Edith Cowan University in Australia, told ABC News that scammers often search community groups for information they can use to target individuals.He explained that artificial intelligence and automated tools have made it easier for scammers to gather information, personalise messages and make fraudulent approaches appear more relevant to their targets.Missing-pet appeals can provide information such as an animal's name, appearance, location and photographs. While sharing these details can help owners reach people who might have seen their pets, the same information can potentially be misused.A manipulated photograph may appear convincing because it features the actual missing animal. However, recognising a pet in an image does not prove that the person sending it has found or possesses the animal.Haskell-Dowland advised people to be cautious about the information they share online, even when they are trying to resolve a distressing situation.The search for Bundy continuesDespite the suspected scam and the disappointment of the failed meeting, Ruyter continued to hope that Bundy would be found.His experience illustrates how a missing-pet appeal can become an opportunity for exploitation when someone uses an owner's public posts to create a convincing but misleading claim.Authorities have warned that scammers can use fabricated images to demand payment from people who are desperate to recover their animals. In Ruyter's case, the suspected deception compounded the distress of an already difficult search.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
