articles.title: Your pay, energy bills and cash Isa: How the Budget affects you
articles.summary: Changes announced by Chancellor John Healey in his first Budget will affect your finances directly. Here's how.
articles.body:
Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.

The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.

Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.

If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.

It will be paid directly into your bank account.

You can find your council tax band by looking on your annual bill, or by looking on the government's website - although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.

Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.

This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that. Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.

The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July. It was due to end in April.

Healey announces £100 energy payment for millions and bank tax rise in first Budget

The fee for connecting to your gas supply so called standing charges will be scrapped in England, Scotland and Wales, next year "or as soon as possible after", the chancellor said.

These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.

The Treasury calculates that 60% of households will save an average of £45 a year, with lower users gaining the most. But the saving will come after the projected big rise in bills in January.

Higher users - in the biggest houses but also large, low-income families - will pay more than they currently do.

The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.

The 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, will be extended to July. It was scheduled to be phased out from January.

It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52.95p per litre.

Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.

The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February. A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.

The chancellor has scrapped his predecessor's plans to reduce the annual amount people can save tax-free in cash in Individual Savings Accounts (Isas).

Rachel Reeves had wanted the policy to encourage personal investment in stocks and shares.

It meant, from April 2027, if you're under 65, you would only be able to save £12,000 a year in cash in an Isa, rather than £20,000.

Instead, the government plans to create a new "Starter Isa" for first-time investors.

If you have a large amount in savings, or if you fail to use the tax-free Isa allowance, then you will pay more tax from April.

You do not pay tax on all savings. There is the annual £20,000 Isa allowance, and an annual savings income allowance (in other words, the interest received on a savings pot) of £1,000 for basic rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers.

But beyond that savings tax rates will rise by four percentage points to 24% and 44% respectively from April.

Landlords could also pay more in tax. In analysis published on Wednesday, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said these steps along with measures over the past decade that have reduced private landlord returns "collectively risk leading to a steady rise in rents".

Minimum wage rise but you'll pay more tax

Minimum wage rates will rise by 3.9% in April. It means:

Eligible workers aged 21 and over on the National Living Wage will receive £13.21 an hour, up from £12.71

If you are aged 18, 19 or 20, the National Minimum Wage will increase to £11.27 an hour, up from £10.85

For those aged 16 or 17, the minimum wage will rise to £8.31 an hour, up from £8

The separate apprentice rate which applies to eligible people under 19 - or those over 19 in the first year of an apprenticeship – will also increase to £8.31 an hour, from £8

However, these figures mean, this time around, there's no progress on Labour's manifesto promise to narrow the gap in minimum wages between older and younger workers.

For all workers, the ongoing freeze in the income bands , or thresholds, at which income tax is paid went unmentioned in the Budget.

But it means any kind of pay rise could drag you into a higher tax bracket, or see a greater proportion of your income taxed than would otherwise be expected. Scotland has its own income tax bands.

How much is the minimum wage going up by?

The triple lock policy means that the state pension will go up in line with average wage increases, at 3.9%.

the flat-rate state pension for those who reached state pension age after April 2016 will be £250.70 a week, or £13,036.40 a year, up £488 on now

the old basic state pension for those who reached state pension age before April 2016 will be £192.10 a week, or £9,989.20 a year, up £374.40 on now

The government had already committed to not taxing people who only get an income from the state pension.

The chancellor said this would be the case until at least 2030, as there will be a new Pension Tax Allowance, so pensioners with an income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax.

The First Time Buyer Isa has been in the planning stages with the government for a while.

Healey has confirmed that it is intended to replace the often-criticised Lifetime Isa.

Separately, he confirmed the Your First Home equity scheme to allow first-time buyers in England to buy a new-build home with a deposit of 2.5%. It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their property's value to help pay for the purchase.

The government has made no changes to student loan rates - saying only that it is being "kept under review".

There has been some backlash after the previous chancellor froze the repayment threshold for Plan 2 student loans, which were given out for just over a decade in England from 2012.

It means the salary at which borrowers start paying back their loans is due to stay at £29,385 in April and remain there for three years – so graduates start repaying sooner and repay more each month than they would otherwise have done.

Some announcements affecting your finances have already been made by the government.

Tariffs removed from 100 food items such as baked beans and garlic, which the government calculates could save households up to £21 per year - or 40p a week - when combined with existing tariff suspensions that were introduced in June

Allowing carers to earn more than an existing earnings limit without losing their entire allowance, replacing it with a taper mechanism instead. However, this will not come in until 2030

Giving two weeks of paternity pay to self-employed fathers, who have previously missed out on payments of up to £194 a week for the period

Making permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above that

The prime minister's plan to reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares in England from January to be in effect throughout 2027. Some cities already have caps, and funding is being given to the devolved nations

articles.title: In 1989, CNN founder Ted Turner removed cattle from his 113,000-acre Montana ranch, replaced them with bison and 'set one unusual rule' when Yellowstone’s wolves arrived
articles.summary: Ted Turner transformed his 113,613-acre Flying D Ranch in Montana after buying the property in 1989, replacing domestic cattle with a managed bison herd
articles.body: Ted Turner transformed his 113,613-acre Flying D Ranch in Montana after buying the property in 1989, replacing domestic cattle with a managed bison herd and pursuing a different approach to wildlife conservation. When wolves dispersing from Yellowstone National Park established a presence on the ranch, Turner made an unusual decision for a working livestock operation: he instructed his staff not to shoot the predators, even if they killed bison, according to Montana Free Press. The property now supports around 4,500 bison, while grassland restoration, forest management and stream conservation form part of a wider effort to protect its wildlife habitat.How Ted Turner transformed his Montana ranch with bison and conservation effortsTurner purchased the 113,613-acre Flying D Ranch near Bozeman in 1989. The property lies between the Gallatin and Madison river systems, an area of open grassland, forest and waterways that forms part of a much larger landscape used by wildlife.After acquiring the ranch, Turner removed its domestic cattle and established a managed bison herd. The animals continued to be raised within a working agricultural operation, rather than being left entirely to their own devices. Montana classifies bison as livestock, so the ranch still requires fencing and active management of grazing areas.The herd has since grown to approximately 4,500 animals, according to the Turner Institute of Ecoagriculture. Ranch management has also included efforts to return former farmland to native grassland. More than 5,000 acres of previously cultivated land have been restored to native grazing habitat, according to information about the property's conservation work.The land itself has protection against future development. Turner placed the ranch under a conservation easement held by The Nature Conservancy, restricting certain forms of development and helping preserve open space and wildlife movement across the region. The easement is among the largest of its kind in Montana.When Yellowstone's wolves began moving onto private landThe return of wolves to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 brought a new element to the management of surrounding ranchland. As the animals spread beyond the park, some established territories on neighbouring properties, including the Flying D.By 2002, wolves dispersing from Yellowstone had established a presence on the ranch. For a commercial livestock operation, their arrival presented a familiar problem: predators could kill animals that had financial value to the owner. Removing the wolves was an option available to many landowners, depending on the applicable wildlife regulations.Turner chose a different course. Working with biologist Mike Phillips, he allowed the wolves to remain and instructed his staff not to shoot them, even if they preyed on the ranch's animals, as reported by Montana Free Press.The decision did not remove the practical difficulties of keeping predators and livestock on the same property. Instead, it meant that the ranch would accept a degree of risk rather than respond to wolf activity by killing the animals. That policy gave biologists an opportunity to observe how wolves behaved in a landscape where a working bison operation continued alongside them.How the Beartrap wolf pack helped scientists study predators on Ted Turner’s ranchThe wolves established a pack known as Beartrap, which eventually became one of the larger packs in the region. Montana Free Press noted its presence drew the attention of wolf researcher Val Asher and other visiting scientists interested in predator behaviour outside the boundaries of a national park.A privately managed ranch offers a different setting from Yellowstone's protected interior. Wildlife must share the landscape with agricultural activities, fencing and other forms of human land use. Observations at the Flying D helped scientists examine how wolves occupied territory and interacted with a managed bison herd under those conditions.Restoring grasslands, forests and waterwaysWolf management formed only one part of the Flying D's wider land-management programme. The property supports a range of native mammals, including elk, moose, mule deer, white-tailed deer, pronghorn, black bears and mountain lions. Grizzly bears also pass through the ranch, while seasonal elk herds can number more than 2,000.According to Turner Enterprises, the property supports nearly all the large native mammal species found in the contiguous United States, with the Canada lynx the exception. The variety of animals reflects the different habitats across the ranch, from open grasslands to wooded uplands and river corridors.Management work extends into the forests. Ranch staff have treated more than 3,000 acres of timber to limit damage associated with mountain pine beetle infestations. Prescribed burns are also used to help prevent conifers from spreading into open grassland, where changes in vegetation can affect habitat and grazing conditions.Waterways have received attention as well. Conservation partners have restored or protected more than 70 miles of connected stream habitat in local watersheds. The work benefits native fish, including westslope cutthroat trout and Arctic grayling. The ranch also maintains a reservoir used to raise Arctic grayling for reintroduction into Montana rivers, contributing to efforts to recover the species.Bald and golden eagles are among the birds that use the river corridors. Taken together, the ranch's grassland, forest and stream projects form a management programme that reaches well beyond the question of whether wolves should be allowed to stay.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'They will fly': MEA on direct India-Taiwan flights after Pakistan blocks airspace over 'One-China' policy
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday indicated that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, amid reports
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday indicated that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, amid reports that Pakistan has barred Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace under its “One China” policy.“My sense is, if there are direct flights then they will fly,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said when asked about the possibility of direct flights between India and Taiwan.The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace, in a move that highlights Islamabad's support for Beijing's position on Taiwan.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif confirmed the country's position to Bloomberg News, saying its aviation policy permits only mainland Chinese airlines to fly over its airspace.“The aviation division follows the One China policy — only mainland China is allowed,” Asif said.“We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan,” he added.Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers. Bloomberg, citing flight-tracking data, reported that China Airlines Ltd and EVA Airways Corp had not flown over Pakistani airspace since the morning of October 25.The restriction came to light after aviation observers noticed that some Taiwanese flights had begun taking longer routes to reach Europe, flying entirely over Russian airspace since the weekend.According to Flightradar24 data, a China Airlines flight from Taipei to Rome on October 24 flew through Russian airspace, bypassing its earlier route through India, Pakistan and Turkmenistan.The move comes as China continues to urge other countries to support its claim that Taiwan is part of its territory. Beijing considers Taiwan a part of China, while Taipei maintains that the island is self-governed and rejects Beijing's claim.Pakistan's decision also underlines its close ties with China, which Islamabad has described as an “iron-clad friendship”. The two countries have maintained an “all-weather” partnership since establishing diplomatic relations in 1951.In January, Pakistan described Taiwan as an “inalienable part” of China and reiterated its commitment to the One China principle.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 8 dead as Cyclone Arnab batters Andhra coast, uproots trees, poles, damages homes
articles.summary: VISAKHAPATNAM/KAKINADA/AMALAPURAM: Eight people have died in parts of Andhra Pradesh after severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and
articles.body: VISAKHAPATNAM/KAKINADA/AMALAPURAM: Eight people have died in parts of Andhra Pradesh after severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts early on Wednesday.The storm triggered heavy rainfall, uprooted hundreds of trees and electric poles, damaged houses and roads, disrupted power supply and communication, and damaged standing crops across coastal districts. More than 20,000 people were evacuated in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh before the cyclone’s arrival.Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday sought the Union government’s support in dealing with the impact of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab. Naidu spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the phone and briefed him on the cyclone and its impact on the state.Two people were killed in Bhimavaram in West Godavari district. In the first incident, Ch Kishore (45) died after a tree fell on him, while Rambabu died after an electric pole collapsed on him.In Konaseema district, K Venkayamma died after a thatched house collapsed on her in Sakenetipalle mandal. Similarly, another woman died in Prakashpuram in Sakenetipalle mandal.In Visakhapatnam city, two women were killed after electric poles collapsed on them in the Goshala and Balajinagar localities. One of the victims was identified as K Madhavi.Further, a 55-year-old woman died after accidentally stepping on an exposed live wire outside her home in Yellamanchili town in Anakapalli district on Wednesday morning.It may be recalled that one person, A Pinni Devudu (65), died of electrocution in the Mangalapalem locality of Vizag city after coming into contact with a live wire that had snapped.Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts to the southwest of Yanam, about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40 km southwest of Yanam and 60 km southwest of Kakinada, between 2 am and 8 am on Wednesday.It crossed the coast as a very severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 125-135 kmph and gusts reaching 150 kmph. The system weakened from a very severe cyclonic storm to a severe cyclonic storm after crossing the coast.The system is likely to move north-northwestwards over the next 48 hours and weaken gradually. It is expected to weaken into a cyclonic storm during the next six hours and further into a deep depression over the subsequent six hours.The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam districts on Thursday (October 29).Konaseema is among the worst-affected districts in Andhra Pradesh, with winds reaching up to 130 kmph. The winds uprooted trees and electric poles, damaged standing paddy and horticultural crops, blocked roads, and disrupted power supply and communication.The cyclone damaged paddy fields in parts of Konaseema district but spared coconut plantations, providing considerable relief to farmers.“The cyclone damaged the paddy fields in parts of Konaseema districts and spared the coconut plantations, which is a huge relief for us as coconut is a commercial crop,” said Ravi, a resident of Perurupeta in Konaseema district.“Though we expected massive devastation due to the cyclone, fortunately, the damage is not as we expected,” he added.As per preliminary estimates, the cyclone uprooted hundreds of trees and around 100 electric poles in Kakinada district. However, no major damage has been reported, and rainfall subsided after 2 am on Wednesday. The Uppada coastal road was completely washed away in Kakinada district.Prolonged power interruptions following Cyclone Arnab have caused considerable hardship to residents in several parts of Konaseema and Kakinada districts, with people in both districts reporting outages lasting more than a day.In Visakhapatnam city, hundreds of trees were also uprooted, while several low-lying areas witnessed waterlogging as the city recorded more than 20 cm of rainfall in 24 hours.Electricity connections were expected to be restored by Wednesday evening in parts of the state, and major highways were expected to be cleared within hours.According to the IMD, Garividi in Vizianagaram district recorded the highest rainfall, at 26 cm, between Tuesday morning and Wednesday morning.This was followed by 25 cm each in Anakapalle, S Kota, Vepada and Cheepurupalle; 24 cm each in Bheemili, Mentada and Yellamanchili; and 23 cm each in Gantyada and Ranastalam.Gajapathinagaram, Nellimarla, Visakhapatnam and Merakamudidam each recorded 22 cm of rainfall. The weather agency reported 21 cm each in Vizianagaram, Chodavaram and Bondapalle, and 20 cm in Denkada.Many parts of the state recorded between 10 cm and 17 cm of rainfall during the period.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: 'Ruthless' podcast breaks down investment by Ohio Democrat in China-linked fund
articles.summary: Greg Landsman's investment in a Chinese military-linked fund drew sharp criticism on the "Ruthless Podcast" as Ohio's midterm election nears.
articles.body: With less than a week until the midterm elections, the "Ruthless" podcast hosts questioned Rep. Greg Landsman's, D-Ohio, reported investment in a fund with holdings in Chinese military-linked companies. "How are you allowed to hold that [fund as] an elected official in this country?" podcast co-host Comfortably Smug asked in an episode released Wednesday morning. "That is stunning." Ohio News previously reported that, according to financial disclosures, Landsman and his wife held between $30,001 and $100,000 in the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF. The Department of War has identified some companies held by the fund as Chinese military companies. DEMS RAKED IN MILLIONS FROM EMPLOYEES AT FIRMS NEWLY IDENTIFIED AS 'CHINESE MILITARY COMPANIES' Podcast co-host Josh Holmes explained the possible national security significance of a congressman owning these types of funds. "The reason why this is significant is the Pentagon puts out a list every year of companies that are associated with national security threats," Holmes said. "If you are a company that wants to contract anywhere in the federal government, if you have holdings in those companies that are on that list, you can't get a government contract. Evidently, you could get elected to Congress." Landsman's campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Washington Free Beacon reported in September that Landsman amended his 2022 financial disclosure nearly three years after filing it, revealing dozens of previously undisclosed stock holdings. In a press release from 2025, Landsman claimed that he sold all of his stocks, mutual funds, and ETFs to become compliant with the TRUST in Congress Act. WALL STREET BANKS HELPED CHINESE MILITARY-LINKED FIRM RAISE BILLIONS DESPITE RED FLAGS, LAWMAKERS FIND EX-HOUSE DEM WHO RIPPED CONGRESSIONAL STOCK TRADING BAN AS 'BULLS---' CHANGES HER TUNE IN COMEBACK BID "I wanted to be one of the first members of Congress to comply with this legislation – even before it becomes law – because people see a system that’s broken, and I’m determined to be part of the generation that fixes it," Landsman said at the time. "I don’t want a single constituent to think that I’m doing anything in DC but thinking about them." Landsman faces Republican Eric Conroy in the general election to represent the 1st Congressional District in southwestern Ohio. Fox News’ latest rankings classified the race as "likely Democratic." Republicans view the seat as an opportunity to expand their narrow majority against the insurgent Democrats. Political eyes have centered on the Buckeye State in recent weeks as Ohians will also vote in a competitive U.S. Senate race that could decide control of the chamber and a hotly contested gubernatorial election. articles.title: APSEZ Q2 PAT rises 18% to Rs 3,682 crore; raises FY27 guidance
articles.summary: APSEZ Q2 PAT rises 18% to Rs 3,682 crore; revenue up 24%. Company raises FY27 revenue to Rs 44,000-46,000 crore and EBITDA to Rs 26,000-27,000 crore.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd (APSEZ) raised its full-year revenue and operating profit guidance after reporting double-digit quarterly profit growth, backed by expansion across its ports, logistics, and marine businesses. Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose 18% year-on-year to Rs 3,682 crore in the Sept quarter.The company increased its FY27 revenue guidance by Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 44,000-46,000 crore. Its EBITDA guidance also rose by Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 26,000-27,000 crore, reflecting its strong first-half performance.Revenue grew 24% to Rs 11,340 crore, while EBITDA increased 23% to Rs 6,807 crore. The revised outlook points to a broader growth strategy beyond domestic port operations. Domestic ports continue to anchor earnings, but international ports, logistics, and marine are driving the company’s expansion.International ports posted the sharpest growth, with revenue up 71% and EBITDA more than tripled. This performance reflected the ramp-up of operations in Colombo and Tanzania, along with a contribution from Australia’s NQXT terminal.Domestic ports remained the largest contributor to earnings. Revenue rose 13%, supported by cargo growth and higher realisations. The business reported an EBITDA margin of 72.5%, providing a stable base as the company expands into other segments.Logistics revenue grew 21%, while marine revenue increased 57%. The logistics business recovered from the disruption caused by the West Asia crisis in the first quarter. Marine growth was supported by fleet expansion, offshore services, and the company’s entry into subsea services.APSEZ said it raised its FY27 capital expenditure guidance by Rs 3,000 crore to Rs 15,000-17,000 crore as it accelerates spending towards its Ambition 2031 targets.The company aims to generate Rs 91,500 crore in revenue and Rs 52,000 crore in EBITDA by FY31. Achieving these targets will require sustained growth across its expanded transport and logistics network.“Domestic ports continue to anchor our earnings, while international ports, logistics and marine are emerging as powerful growth engines,” said Ashwani Gupta, whole-time director and chief executive officer of APSEZ.The key test will be whether the newer growth engines can sustain their expansion and improve their contribution to earnings as capital expenditure rises.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: India team for Hong Kong Sixes 2026: Krunal Pandya to lead the seven-member squad
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar will lead India's seven-member squad at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026.
articles.body:
Krunal Pandya will lead the Indian team for the 2026 Hong Kong Sixes tournament.

The tournament will take place from October 30 to November 1, with India returning to the tournament following a poor performance in the last installment.

Pandya will lead India after Bhuvneshwar Kumar was called up for the T20I series in New Zealand, and Kulwant Khejroliya has taken his place in the seven-man squad.

India are in Group C with Pakistan and the UAE, and they open their campaign against their arch-rivals on Friday, October 30, before facing the UAE the next morning.

India's seven-member squad for the tournament is:

Everyone except Shashank Singh from this team has played at the international level for India, but Rahul Tewatia hasn't played for the senior side despite receiving a national call-up in the past.

The Hong Kong Sixes is an event that features six-a-side matches which are supposed to be quick, fast and highly scoring games.

This event comprises only six players per team. The Hong Kong Sixes was staged in 1992 for the first time. It was last held in 2024 after some absence from the schedule.

India return to Hong Kong Sixes after 2025 exit

India will aim to better their performance from the 2025 event, where they started off strong with a two-run DLS win against Pakistan before going down to Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates.

Pakistan are the defending champions of the 2026 event, having beaten Kuwait in last year's final to clinch their sixth Hong Kong Sixes crown.

This edition will see the participation of eight leading nations along with four Associate Members, all of which will take part in the event at Mission Road Ground or Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground in Mong Kok (MK), Hong Kong.

India have been drawn in Pool C alongside defending champions Pakistan and the UAE.

The top-ranked side from all the four pools will qualify for the Cup semi-final, with the second- and third-placed sides going into the Plate and Bowl competitions, respectively.

Should India top the pool of Pool C, their Cup finals semi-final against Group A winners will take place on October 31, at 12:40 p.m. IST. The final of the Cup will be on November 1, at 12:40 p.m. IST.

The second and third-placed teams from the group stage will play in the Plate finals and Bowl finals, respectively.

articles.title: Will I get the £100 energy payment and when will I receive it?
articles.summary: Here is what you need to know about the payment that millions will receive from January.
articles.body:
Up to 20 million households in England will get a £100 payment directly into their bank accounts this winter, the government has announced.

Here's what you need to know about the payment.

For many people, the £100 on offer is a lot of money, but it's worth considering the context.

A typical yearly energy bill is forecast to jump by £276 in January , so many people will still feel worse off despite the payment.

Will I get the payment? And how can I check?

Those living in properties which are in council tax bands A to D in England will get the payment, the government has said.

As such, it's worth checking which council tax band your home is in . If you live in England, you can use the search function by typing your postcode into the box.

Will I get it if I live in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?

Chancellor John Healey said in his Budget on Wednesday that the policy was for England but that funding is available for Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland to make the payment as well.

Healey urged the Scottish, Welsh, and Northern Irish governments to follow suit "give people of all nations in the UK breathing space on their energy bills this winter".

However, Healey ultimately does not have the power to give the payment to people in the UK outside of England because it will be done through council tax, which is a devolved matter.

Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

How do I get the money? And will I get it if I'm a student or don't pay council tax?

The money will appear in the bank account which you pay council tax with from the start of January.

Students living in halls will not get the payment because student halls are not in council tax bands A to D.

However, if you're a student living in a property which is council tax bands A to D, as in a private home or flat let out by a landlord, you will get the payment.

Students do not pay council tax, so the money cannot go straight into the account they pay council tax with.

As such, the government said the local authority will be responsible for finding a way of giving the payment to the students.

This is also the case for those who do not pay council tax because of another kind of exemption or if you do pay council tax but you do it by cash or some other way.

The government said it will give councils guidance on how local authorities should do this in due course.

Do I have to spend the money on my energy bill?

The government has announced that the money will appear directly in people's accounts, but the cash payments have not been targeted.

As such, people could choose to spend the money on something else.

How is the government funding this payment?

The government said the money for the £100 cash payments is coming from a rise taxes on banks.

The surcharge on bank's corporation tax will rise from 3% to 6% for 15 months from 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2028, the government said.
